temperature.title: Flash it, vent it, cool it
temperature.description: Boiler blowdown leaves at boiler pressure and saturation temperature. Entering the vented tank tangentially, part of it flashes to steam (released through the vent) and the rest drops to ≈ 100 °C. Cooling water is added so the drain to the sewer stays below the permitted temperature (often ≤ ≈ 40–60 °C, local rules). The tank must never be pressurised: the vent is sized for the flash flow and must not be valved.

video_tutorials.title: Blowdown Tank — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Blowdown Tank.
A boiler blowdown tank receives water blown down from boilers at high pressure and temperature.
Entering tangentially, part of it flashes to steam that leaves through a large vent; the rest is retained, mixed with cooling water and drained at a safe temperature to the sewer.
Typical applications include continuous and intermittent (bottom) boiler blowdown; drain collection from high-pressure steam traps and drains.
The cutaway reveals the internal construction.
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

video_tutorials.title: Blowdown Tank — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Blowdown Tank.
Check vent is clear; discharge temperature.
Inspect wear plate and shell thickness.
Repair erosion areas.
Watch for tank pressurised: steam leaks, overpressure. Common cause: vent blocked or undersized.
Watch for shell erosion: thinning at inlet. Common cause: worn wear plate.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
